findings.resolution: The concrete pinned local-Git producer replays repository bytes, while current R0.2/R0.1 replay revalidates raw and normalized graph, ontology/profile, edge artifacts, policies and time. Caller mappings, seeds and path subsets are absent.

Every complete bytewise non-delete change maps exactly once through an exact canonical locator to one unique source-artifact anchor. Unmapped, duplicate, ambiguous, aliased and unsafe locators block the aggregate.

Stable ordered-topology path identities separate semantic scope from time-varying R0.1/R0.2 receipt hashes. Verification first binds historical audit roots, then recompiles and compares the stable current projection.
Final UTC is sampled after nested replay, nested chronology and expiry are checked against it, and graph/change/locator plus aggregate seed/path capacities fail closed without truncation.

Artifacts and evaluations are hard-typed ANALYSIS_ONLY and release-ineligible and retain graph-input, change-seed, build, deploy, risk, obligation, execution, conflict, approval, source, origin, signature and global interlock gaps.
A same-tree graph-producer receipt, candidate/base graph linkage and deleted-artifact tombstones remain mandatory before mapping can become change-seed attestation. The capability remains FOUNDATION.

Genuine rebuilt-graph permutations, broader multi-file diamond/cycle cases and direct capacity-boundary regressions remain nonblocking hardening because current authority and pinned upstream caps already fail closed.
